traits.note: Watson and Dallwitz, The Families of Flowering Plants (DELTA data, items edited May 2026), family Anisophylleaceae: leaves alternate; leaves simple; veins palmate; stipules absent; plants usually monoecious, rarely hermaphrodite; ovary inferior; stems woody; flowers in panicles or in racemes, rarely solitary; flowers actinomorphic; perianth sepals and petals; fruit usually drupe, rarely capsule or samara; parts of each whorl (2-) 3 to 4 (-5); stamens 8; carpels (3-) 4. Read from the coded states by script (spec-rework/b1/delta/mapdelta.py); a state the authors qualify (rarely, usually, a share) keeps its word, an unqualified one beside a usual state reads as sometimes.
